name: media-result
title: Media Result
description: A finished piece of generated media, with its provenance attached. Takes the media itself as children, a `title`, an `aspectRatio` so the layout never jumps, `madeBy` naming the model and time, a `credentials` object (`attached`, a `detail` such as "Content Credentials + invisible watermark", and an optional `href` to verify), a `note` for usage rights, and `actions` with `onAction`. Provenance is stated in words beside the result rather than hidden in a details panel, and when credentials are **not** attached the frame says so plainly, because an unmarked file is the one a team needs to know about before it ships. That reflects the law as of August 2026: the EU AI Act's Article 50 and California's SB 942 both require machine-readable disclosure of AI-generated media, and the major generators now sign output with C2PA credentials and an invisible watermark. Purely presentational: you render the media and own the signing. Use it wherever a generated image, video or audio clip is presented as finished. Not for work still in progress (that is Generation Job), and not for a grid of candidates (that is Variation Grid).

meta.engineeringNotes: `credentials` is a small object rather than a boolean because the three questions a team has are different: is it signed, what was applied, and where can it be checked. Treating the unsigned case as a visible state in the waiting colour — instead of simply omitting the line — is the deliberate inversion here: products that only show a badge when signing succeeds make an unsigned file indistinguishable from a file nobody thought about, which is precisely the one that must not ship under the 2026 disclosure rules. The frame is a `figure` with a `figcaption`, so provenance and title are associated with the media by the platform rather than by proximity, and the whole caption stays outside the media box so it is never baked into a screenshot of the image itself.
meta.motionNotes: Nothing animates: the work is finished, and this system reserves motion for a machine that is still busy. Only the standard instant colour changes on the action buttons, dropped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

children.description: The result itself: an `img`, a `video`, an audio player. Yours to render.

title.description: What it is, in the user's words: "Bottle on stone, warm light".

aspectRatio.description: Aspect ratio of the frame, so the layout never jumps while media loads.

madeBy.description:
What made it and when, formatted by you. Shown with the result, not hidden in a
details panel.

attached.description: True once your pipeline has signed the file.

detail.description: "Content Credentials + SynthID", "C2PA manifest signed by Acme".

credentials.description:
Content Credentials (C2PA) and any visible or invisible watermark. Since August 2026
the EU AI Act's Article 50 and California's SB 942 both require machine-readable
disclosure of AI-generated media, so this is a product requirement, not a nicety.

note.description: Your own note: usage rights, model terms, "for internal use".

UINode.description: A nested component: a name from this catalogue, and the props to give it.

props.description: That component's own props, matching its entry in this catalogue.

primary.description: The one action that takes the result forward. At most one.

docs: Requires `cn` at `@/lib/utils`. Render the media yourself and give images real alt text. Pass `credentials.attached: false` honestly — the absence is the useful signal.
